correctness.rationale: For a nonzero last-layer element a, locality and nilpotence give l(a)=J, so Ra is simple. Writing Ra=l(c) forces c in J and J^{n-1}=l(c). Right multiplication by c embeds J^i/J^{n-1} into J^{i+1}, yielding finite left length by downward induction. Since R/J^{n-1} is isomorphic to Rc and J has the same finite length, Rc=J; c is nilpotent and the standard left-special criterion applies.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Camillo--Nicholson explicitly posed the local nilpotent-radical question in 2015. Targeted searches under pseudo-morphic, principal-annihilator and CEFR terminology did not locate a resolution. The main residual risk is the uninspected full text of the 2023 CEFR paper or differently phrased equivalent literature.

value.rationale: The theorem affirmatively resolves an explicit published question and strengthens it: a single nonzero pseudo-morphic element in the last radical layer already forces the ring to be left special. The proof also derives finite left length rather than assuming it.
